findings.finding: The table gives two base answers that point in opposite directions. The fair value row says 163$ (31% expensive), but the yearly base path is worth 219.5$ at year 0 and 239$ at year 1 (+12%/yr): the same scenario, the same Ke of 9.95%, 35% apart. The gap comes from how each method treats reinvestment. The DCF base reinvests 1.71bn in 2027 as capex (maintenance 0.36bn + growth 1.36bn, 9.7% of revenue). That matches the register's exe.capex_plan (8.8% versus 2.2% historically) but contradicts the company's own 2026 capex guide of $550-570m (about 4% of sales; field fd_bn_capacity). The DCF also locks a minimum cash of 2.81bn (all of the June 2026 cash, an assumption without company data) and fades to a terminal reinvestment rate of 41% (terminal ROIC about 12%). The result is base 2027 FCFE of 0.79bn, 4.5% of revenue, against FY2025 FCF of 18.5%. The path instead keeps ROIC at 30% to the terminal. An independent expectation_gap run with the base drivers (revenue0 14.0bn, g1 0.26 for 3 years, margin 0.19->0.20, sales_to_capital 2.2, tax 23%, WACC 9.5%, UIG 1.45bn cash and 234.6m earnout deducted) gives about 200$ a share (-6% versus 213$). That sits near the path, not the 163$ DCF. So the headline 'expensive by 31%' and the 132$ buy-below row rest on an engine reinvestment and cash-buffer choice that has no company evidence.

findings.finding: Counter-thesis (pre-mortem, October 2029: the stock is down 50-70%). (1) 2027-28 brings a data-center capex digestion at hyperscalers and neoclouds (CoreWeave, Nebius named as a 'material part' of customers). Neocloud funding tightens, and because VRT stopped disclosing orders, backlog and book-to-bill in 2026 (flag backlog_disclosure_dropped), the slowdown shows up only as missed revenue after the $15.0bn backlog ships. (2) Eaton (Electrical Global backlog +103%), Schneider, Legrand and Delta bring their added capacity and liquid cooling on line, so the scarcity premium that took Q2 2026 GAAP margin to 19.5% (6-year median 12.7%, flag peak_margin_run_rate) reverts. (3) The $1.82bn of H1 2026 customer advances (flag customer_advances_inflate_cash) reverse, so 2027 FCF collapses while management's annual incentive is paid on adjusted FCF that those advances flatter (flag incentive_on_adjusted_fcf). (4) Growth is increasingly bought: PurgeRite 1.14bn, UIG 1.45bn + up to 1.15bn earnout, King Environmental. Net cash turns to net debt, earnout liabilities (234.6m, -62m fair-value loss in H1 2026) rise, and goodwill impairments follow. (5) The multiple derates from about 36x FY2026 GAAP EPS. What would have shown it early: sequential decline in current deferred revenue, Q4 2026 / FY2027 organic sales guide below 20%, an adjusted operating margin guide below 22%, competitor data-center order or backlog deceleration (ETN, SU, LR, Delta quarterly reports), further earnout fair-value losses, and EMEA continuing to shrink while Schneider and Legrand grow.

findings.finding: The bear does not model what its own lead event says. The event says orders stop after the current backlog ships, yet bear revenue still grows 6% in 2027 and 4.5-5% every year after (14.83bn, 15.70bn, 16.48bn, 17.31bn in 2027-2030), with no down year. With a material share of sales from hyperscale and neocloud customers and the backlog runoff largely complete within 12-18 months, a real capex pause would show a revenue decline in 2028. The bear's damage comes almost entirely from margin (to 14%) and the multiple (14.2x forward against an own-history trailing low of 38.3x). rk.bear_levers shows dilution, financing, discount and capex not modeled in the bear: the bear funding equals the base (debt 4,624m flat, SBC 0.5%), and the UIG earnout of up to 1.15bn is absent (only 234.6m is a claim). The generic permanent_loss:utilization_collapse (5.43$) is not company-sized.

findings.finding: The base is not clearly the most likely path; it leans conservative without company evidence for the margin. Base FY2027 GAAP EPS is 6.42, only +9% on the FY2026 GAAP guide midpoint of 5.87, while revenue grows 26%. That means the 2027 operating margin after SBC (19.1%) falls below the 2026 run rate, against a Q2 2026 adjusted margin of 22.6% and a Q3 guide of 24-25%. The only support is a qualitative reading on competitor capacity. Attributed consensus, which is an expectation and not evidence, is FY2027 revenue 18.27bn (n=30, low 17.24bn) and FY2027 adjusted EPS 9.19 (low 8.28). Adding back the FY2026 GAAP-to-adjusted gap of about 0.86, base adjusted EPS is about 7.3, below the lowest of 30 estimates. That should be stated next to the table.

findings.finding: What the price assumes (expectation_gap, each lever alone, base anchor as above, which gives about 200$). At 213$ the price needs one of the following. Growth of 27.8% for 3 years instead of 26%; this sets a 5-year revenue CAGR of 25.2% against a demonstrated 3-year CAGR of 21.6%. Or a mature EBIT margin after SBC of 21.0% against the best reported GAAP year of 17.9% (FY2025) and TTM of 18.9%. Or sales-to-capital of 2.87 against the 2.06 implied by 2020-2025 invested capital. Every lever needs more than the company has shown, but only modestly above the base, so the price is roughly consistent with the base drivers. The real disagreement is margin durability: the price needs a margin above any full reported year, held to maturity. This is the counter-thesis lever, yet only the bear contains a margin drop. The engine's own WMBT (25.6% versus 18.0% five-year average growth) uses a different base growth path from the analyst's 26% 2027 anchor fading. The table row 'what the price assumes' (about 12% real growth for 10 years, 7% base rate) should be read with that in mind. redteam_audit (casefile rk.redteam): passed, with critical_failed and critical_unverifiable empty. But its cash, debt and shares checks pass by construction (by_construction: cash_reconciles, debt_complete, shares_current), dataqa post_period_events is missing, and shares are the cover count of 2026-07-27 (93 days old). It is not an independent pass.
